notes:
26 rows, 13 starred (95, 98, 99, 101, 102, 105, 106, 108, 109, 115, 117, 118, 119). That matches the lead-in on lines 88-89 ("twenty-six lighthouses ... Thirteen stations have sent in returns").

Keeper count: 20 of the 26 rows name a keeper, not 18 as the other reader said. The six rows without a name are Whalsey Skerries, Bressay Sound, Start Point, Cantick Head, Chanonry Point and Covesea Skerries. Holborn Head, Cromarty, Kinnaird Head, Buchan Ness, Montroseness and St. Abbs Head name a keeper but are not starred. So a named keeper does not mean a return came in.

Coast: the section heading is printed "_EAST COAST OF SCOTLAND._" (line 84, italic). I gave it as "EAST COAST OF SCOTLAND" without the underscores and the full stop. There are no sub-headings in the list. No row prints a map number or a type (L.H./L.V.), so number and type are null everywhere.

Fragments leave out the list's leading indentation (2-3 spaces, and 7 before the ditto mark on line 103) but are otherwise exact. In marks, "*" is the return star; no row has an italic name.

Ditto row (line 103): printed '"     (High) Orkney' with no comma between "(High)" and "Orkney", unlike every other row. It stands for Hoy Sound (High). Its name is given as printed, '"     (High)'.

Spellings and placements kept as printed but worth checking: "Whalsey" (Whalsay); "North Ronaldshay" (Ronaldsay); "Tarbet Ness" (Tarbat Ness); "Inch Keith" (Inchkeith); "Girdleness" and "Montroseness" are each one word (Montrose Ness is usually called Scurdie Ness). "Bressay Sound" is the light usually called Bressay. Chanonry Point is placed in "Elgin", but it is on the Ross-shire side of the Moray Firth, so the county looks wrong. Cromarty is printed "E. Cromarty". Keeper names that may be misprints: "Alex. Creig" (Craig?), "Wm. Gulcher", "Alex. Harp".

Character text: abbreviations are kept as printed ("rev.", "int.", "½ m.", "2½ m.", "10 sec."). Holborn Head, Noss Head and Tarbet Ness end in an abbreviation, so I kept the full stop, since it belongs to the abbreviation and not the sentence. For the other rows the full stop before the keeper's name is the sentence's, so I left it out. Bell Rock's "white and red revolving" has no comma, as printed. An earlier commit already flags Chanonry Point's 1879 character as a slip compared with Findlay 1879.
